page: Microsoft Azure E2_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance utilizes an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 2 vCPUs sourced from 1 physical core via hyperthreading, alongside 16.0 GB of memory, which establishes an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Cache allocation includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. Supported instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI, alongside hardware cryptography acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance provision contains no local disk storage and lacks GPU acceleration.

Performance benchmarks reflect steady single-threaded capability accompanied by low overall parallel capacity due to the two-thread ceiling. Single-core evaluations show competitive midrange behavior, recording 1631.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1889.38 in stress-ng, alongside 28.21 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks reflect the hardware limits of a single physical core, scoring 1873.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 1931.79 in stress-ng multi-core tests. Memory throughput registers at 14.91 GB/sec for uncached reads and 13.55 GB/sec for uncached writes, yielding 1.98 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.78 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary operational tradeoff of the E2_v5 lies in its high memory-to-core ratio contrasted with minimal multithreaded capacity and complete reliance on remote storage. Because the instance pairs 16.0 GB of RAM with only two processing threads, it provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound tasks that do not justify paying for additional compute cores. Workload suitability centers on small caching layers, lightweight relational databases, message queues, and low-traffic background ETL services.
description: Microsoft Azure E2_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for applications requiring high memory density relative to core count. Built on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, the instance delivers 2 vCPUs from a single hyperthreaded physical core alongside 16.0 GB of RAM. The instance does not include local disk storage or GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage. In benchmark evaluations, it demonstrates steady single-core compute performance, with midrange results in single-threaded stress-ng and Geekbench runs, though aggregate multi-core throughput is constrained by the two-thread limit. Memory throughput reaches 14.91 GB/sec for uncached reads, supporting up to 1.98 million Redis SET operations per second. The E2_v5 provides cost-efficient deployment for memory-dependent tasks that require minimal CPU concurrency, such as lightweight database engines, caching layers, low-traffic web serving, and basic ETL processing.
